Over 2,950 free-ranging dogs (FRDs) were sterilised with the aim of saving Black-necked Cranes (BNC) and boosting wildlife tourism-based livelihoods in Ladakh under the initiative of Bombay Natural History Society (BNHS) along with the Indian Army, the Animal Husbandry Department, and the Department of Forest, Ecology and Environment.
The initiative started in 2022 to conserve BNC chicks, after the wildlife expert noticed that FRDs have been killing them in the Alpine Wetlands of Ladakh and preventing BNCs from settling down in one place for nesting.
BNC, globally listed as “vulnerable”, is a cultural symbol and state Bird of Ladakh, but fewer than 100 survive in India, while the estimated world population is roughly 11,000–12,000 individuals, most of which occur on the Tibetan Plateau. They are distributed across four range countries—India, Nepal, Bhutan, and China.
According to BNHS authorities, 110–130 individuals are recorded annually, including 20–25 breeding pairs, depending on the year. The main breeding sites include the Changthang Cold Desert Wildlife Sanctuary, the wetlands of Hanle, Tso Kar, Nyoma, and nearby marshes, with an extended population in the Suru Valley. “During the annual population monitoring conducted in early June 2026, a total of 19 pairs of BNC were recorded across the wetlands of Ladakh,” said Kishor Rithe, Director of BNHS.
However, BNHS scientist Dr Muhammad Raza, working in Ladakh, informed that the actual number of pairs is expected to be slightly higher, saying, “Due to logistical challenges and limited accessibility, several sites could not be surveyed. BNHS is taking necessary measures to get a clear picture of the breeding population of BNC in Ladakh.”
Efforts under the initiative
BNC has been facing threats across its breeding habitats due to increased human use of areas surrounding wetlands, expansion of linear infrastructure, habitat degradation, FRDs, and the impacts of climate change.
To address disturbance to nesting birds at the hands of FRDs, BNHS led the initiative, which also includes efforts to reduce the availability of anthropogenic food subsidies. A pilot waste-management project has been initiated at selected Indian Army outposts to improve the handling and disposal of food and kitchen waste, thereby limiting access to food resources that sustain FRD populations.
“By integrating waste management with sterilisation efforts, the programme seeks to provide a long-term and sustainable approach to reducing dog-related threats in ecologically sensitive wetland landscapes,” said a BHNS authority.
Additionally, capacity-building and awareness programmes have been launched, and 1,000 armed forces personnel have been trained in biodiversity conservation and wildlife management.

Vice President C.P. Radhakrishnan on Wednesday (August 12, 2026) said the national song Vande Mataram played a crucial role in awakening patriotism among Indians and uniting people across regions, languages, faiths and social backgrounds during the freedom struggle.
Addressing the 'Har Ghar Tiranga' bike rally commemorating 150 years of Vande Mataram at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi, Mr. Radhakrishnan said the two words "Vande Mataram" had "lightened the burning patriotism in the minds of every Indian in those days", becoming the prime force that uprooted the British colonial Raj from India.
"Our freedom struggle was an awakening of the Indian mind, the Indian spirit, and the Indian consciousness. It united people across regions, languages, faiths, and social backgrounds through a shared dream of freedom, a shared dream of one India," he said.
Mr. Radhakrishnan said when Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay penned the immortal words, he "gave voice to the soul of the nation wanting to breathe freedom".
"For our countless freedom fighters, this song was more than just words. They were a source of courage, sacrifice, and hope," he said, adding that many freedom fighters went to the gallows with "Vande Mataram" in their hearts.
Referring to the special discussion held in Parliament on the 150th anniversary of Vande Mataram, Mr. Radhakrishnan said the deliberation lasted more than 12 hours and was "one of the most engaging and meaningful deliberations of the session".
He said it was particularly significant for him as it took place during his "very first session as the presiding officer of Rajya Sabha".
Recalling his recent visit to the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Mr. Radhakrishnan said he visited the place where Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose had hoisted the Tricolour in 1943 and proclaimed the islands free from colonial rule.
Mr. Radhakrishnan said he also visited the Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose Island and the historic Cellular Jail, where several freedom fighters were kept in solitary confinement.
He said many of the brave inmates of the Cellular Jail walked to the gallows singing Vande Mataram. "Their courage and sacrifice continue to inspire every generation of our country," he said.
"Vande Mataram is a call that transformed love for one's motherland into a national duty," Mr. Radhakrishnan said, adding that the sentiment spread "like wildfire from Bengal to every nook and corner of Mother Bharat".
He said India was now "marching confidently towards the vision set by our Prime Minister Narendra Modi, a Viksit Bharat by 2047".
The 'Har Ghar Tiranga' bike rally was particularly meaningful as, in the 150th year of Vande Mataram, "we are taking the spirit of that song back to the streets", the Vice President said.
He said the country was now witnessing the fifth edition of 'Har Ghar Tiranga', which was launched by Prime Minister Narendra Modi in 2022, and the initiative has become "a people's movement".
"The strength of the Har Ghar Tiranga movement lies in the fact that the nation is not asking citizens to watch a celebration. It is inviting them to be a part of it," he said.
Citizens across the country were participating in Tiranga yatras, bike and cycle rallies, cultural programmes and concerts, he said, adding, "Each activity has a different form, but the sentiment behind them is common. The national flag is the symbol in which every citizen can find a sense of longing."
Union Minister of Culture and Tourism Gajendra Singh Shekhawat, Union Minister for Social Justice and Empowerment Virendra Kumar, Union Minister of State for Science and Technology Dr. Jitendra Singh, Union Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju, and Union Minister of Coal and Mines G Kishan Reddy were among those present.

Rape survivors, with pregnancies up to 24 weeks, do not require the permission from a court to seek a legal termination of pregnancy, the Madhya Pradesh High Court has said.
A Single Bench of Justice Sandeep N. Bhatt in Indore on August 11 made the remarks hearing a petition filed by the father of a 16-year-old sexual assault survivor who sought the court’s approval for the girl’s 18-week pregnancy. The petition cited extreme mental trauma for the survivors to continue with the pregnancy.
Saying that the matter did not require court intervention, Justice Bhatt disposed off the plea while citing a February 20, 2025, verdict that the High Court’s Division Bench in Jabalpur had earlier clarified that under the provisions of the Medical Termination of Pregnancy (MTP) Act, 1971, survivors of sexual assault, rape, or incest, with pregnancies up to 24 weeks, who want to undergo an abortion do not require judicial proceedings under Article 226 of the Constitution.
The court also issued directions to State’s Health Commissioner to communicate the Jabalpur Bench’s judgement to hospitals in the State for future reference.
“The Commissioner, Health Department, may also communicate the aforesaid order passed by the Division Bench to all the concerned hospitals more particularly the Government Hospitals, so that they can also take care of the situation in future,” the Indore Bench order read.
“With the above directions, since no intervention is required in the matter, present petition is dismissed,” it said.
In February, 2025, the Division Bench headed by the then Chief Justice Suresk Kumar Kait had laid out standard operating procedures (SOPs) to be followed by concerned officials and medical officers while dealing with pregnancies of rape or incest survivors for both cases where the pregnancy is of less than 24 weeks and beyond it.
It had asked the authorities to not demand any legal or magisterial requisition or other documentation as a pre-requisite in cases with pregnancies up to 24 weeks, while saying that court’s permission was only required if the pregnancy is of more than 24 weeks.

The Piler police in Annamayya district on Wednesday (August 12, 2026) night arrested a 41-year-old woman and a man on charges of murdering her husband, whom they allegedly saw as an obstacle to their relationship.
Superintendent of Police Dheeraj Kunubilli said the accused, Mangineni Umadevi of Piler town and Charala Subrahmanyam, 32, of Chandragiri in Tirupati district, allegedly planned the murder and attempted to pass it off as a road accident.
On August 7, Umadevi allegedly mixed sleeping pills supplied by Charala Subrahmanyam in the breakfast she gave her husband, Mangineni Venkata Subrahmanyam, 46. After he fell unconscious, Charala Subrahmanyam was allegedly called to the house, and the two allegedly killed her husband with an iron rod and a stone.
The SP said the two later carried the body on a scooter and left it on the Madanapalle-Tirupati highway. The police recovered the weapons used and the blood-stained clothes.

A special MP-MLA court has allowed the prosecution to withdraw a case against 25 BJP leaders and Hindu activists, including Uttar Pradesh Minister Kapil Dev Agarwal, former Union Minister Sanjeev Balyan and former State Minister Suresh Rana, in connection with a 2013 Muzaffarnagar riots-related case.
Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate/MP-MLA court judge Devendra Kumar Faujdar allowed the prosecution's application seeking withdrawal of the case on Wednesday, prosecution officer Rahul Singh said.
The accused were facing trial for allegedly violating prohibitory orders, obstructing public servants in the discharge of their duties, and inciting communal tension through speeches at a mahapanchayat held at Nagla Mador in the district on July 31, 2013, Mr. Singh told PTI on Thursday (August 13, 2026).
The accused included Mr. Agarwal, Mr. Balyan, Mr. Rana, former Uttar Pradesh Minister Ashok Kataria, former BJP MPs Bhartendu Singh and Sohanvir Singh, former BJP MLAs Ashok Kansal and Umesh Malik, VHP leader Sadhvi Prachi and Narsinghanand of Dasna Shiv Temple, among others.
The prosecution moved the application following the Uttar Pradesh government's decision to withdraw the case, Mr. Singh said.
The 2013 Muzaffarnagar riots and subsequent violence in neighbouring districts left more than 60 people dead and displaced over 40,000, according to official figures.

A Karnataka Health Department Food Safety Division team resumed inspection of eateries and other establishments in Bengaluru on Wednesday (August 12, 2026).
The team inspected the canteen at the department’s headquarters in Bengaluru, where it seized expired food items and flagged hygiene violations.
Officials inspected hotels and other food business establishments located in the premises of Vidhana Soudha, Legislators’ Home and the MS Building in Bengaluru.
According to officials, expired food products, such as idli rava and coconut powder, were found in the kitchen of the Arogya Soudha canteen on Magadi Road. Food products were not stored in accordance with FSSAI guidelines. Pest control measures had not been carried out, leaving the premises in an unhygienic condition, officials said.
In a statement, the Food Safety and Drug Administration department said an advisory notice was issued in view of the unhygienic conditions observed at the canteen. Legal proceedings will be initiated before the Adjudicating Officer, it stated.
During inspection of a Nandini parlour located in the premises, officials found violations relating to labelling requirements, and issued an advisory notice, according to the statement.
Four hotels located in the premises of government buildings were inspected, with various deficiencies observed. Advisory notices were issued to the hotels concerned, according to the department.
Officials inspected a restaurant run by a private operator inside Legislators’ House, adjacent to Vidhana Soudha, and found unhygienic conditions. An advisory notice was issued. Among other things, cockroaches were found in the kitchen, they claimed.
A hotel located in the premises of the MS Building was inspected. The establishment was found to be unhygienic and was subsequently closed, the department stated.
The food business operator submitted an undertaking stating that the deficiencies would be rectified and that the hotel would be reopened only after obtaining permission from the Commissioner, in accordance with the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, and the applicable rules, it stated.
Action would be initiated against the food business operator, the department added.
Eateries told to comply with food safety rules
Food business operators have been instructed to strictly comply with the Food Safety and Standards Act and the applicable rules and regulations, the department said.
Any violation relating to food quality, safety, hygiene, proper storage, labelling or food handling practices would invite strict legal action under the law, it added.
The department has been conducting such drives as part of special food safety inspections across all zones of Bengaluru Urban District and the Greater Bengaluru Area, covering three-star and five-star hotels to verify compliance with the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, and the Food Safety and Standards (Licensing and Registration of Food Businesses) Regulations, 2011.
Recently, 60 three-star and five-star hotels in Bengaluru Urban District were inspected, and 77 food samples were collected and sent to food laboratories for analysis.

The Assam Pradesh Congress Committee (APCC) on Wednesday (August 13, 2026) submitted a memorandum to Prime Minister Narendra Modi, urging him to declare the state's recurring flood and river erosion crisis a 'national problem'.
A delegation led by Pranjit Das, Chairman of the APCC Relief & Rehabilitation Department, met Assam Governor Lakshman Prasad Acharya and submitted the memorandum in this regard.
The flood situation in Assam improved on Wednesday (August 13, 2026) as the number of affected people dipped to 87,000 in four districts, but the toll climbed to 103 as two more deaths were reported.
In the memorandum, the Congress said around 40% of Assam's total land area, or 31.05 lakh hectares, is flood-prone, much higher than the national average of 10.2%.
It cited heavy siltation in the Brahmaputra and Barak basins, torrential monsoon rains, shallow riverbeds, embankment breaches and climate change impacts as key factors aggravating the situation.
The crisis has destroyed the livelihoods of farmers, daily wage labourers and tea garden workers, and displaced countless families, it added.
The APCC said the scale of the problem is beyond the capacity of the State government alone and demanded that the Centre recognise it as a "national problem" to ensure a permanent and scientific solution.
The party urged the Centre to set up a high-level task force comprising central and State officials, scientists, technical experts and representatives of affected people to find a solution to the perennial problem.
It also sought adequate central funds for a comprehensive master plan covering river course regulation, embankment strengthening, scientific dredging, real-time flood forecasting, early warning systems and planned rehabilitation of displaced families.
The memorandum further stressed the need for effective coordination among central ministries for integrated management of the Brahmaputra and its tributaries.
"Temporary relief alone cannot provide a lasting solution to this long-standing crisis," it added.

On the last day of the Parliament Monsoon Session on Thursday (August 13, 2026), Leader of the Opposition Mallikarjun Kharge in the Rajya Sabha condemned the ‘shuddhikaran’ (purification) ceremony reportedly held at Haldwani’s Ramlila Ground after he addressed a rally there on Saturday (August 8).
Uttarakhand Congress president Ganesh Godiyal alleged that the Shri Ram Sena, which conducted the ritual, had links to the BJP and the purification was done because Mr. Kharge is a Dalit. He accused the BJP of promoting caste-based divisions and described the incident as deeply objectionable.
“If Kharge ji is insulted, that means everyone is insulted,” said Rajya Sabha Chairman C.P. Radhakrishnan before allowing Mr. Kharge to speak on the incident.
Parliament Monsoon Session Day 19 updates
“I say, with a lot if regret, that I went to deliver a public address at Haldwani. At that time, I did not take any religion’s name, only brought up people’s issues. After my speech, people of the BJP did a “shuddikaran”. Is this the way in democracy? How are you protecting the Constitution?” Mr. Kharge said, amid uproar.
Nadda says enquiry will be initiated
Leader of the House J.P. Nadda slammed the ‘shuddhikaran’ (purification) ceremony, saying that an enquiry will be initiated into the incident and action will be taken against the people involved. Mr. Nadda said, “What Kharge said, it is truly unfortunate. Not just for the Congress, but for all of us.”
Claiming that BJP does not subscribe to such activity, Mr. Nadda said, “Because he said they were BJP people, I want to clarify that the BJP does not subscribe to such activities. But because of the claims, we will investigate. National President Nitin Nabin will take this seriously. We apologise for the hurt it has caused to you.”
“I did not want to make this a political matter. I am in the House for so many years but have never sought sympathy over belonging to the Dalit community,” Mr. Kharge responded. He also demanded a case to be registered under the Untouchability Act, saying, “Register a case against this act of untouchability. That is my demand,” Mr. Kharge said.

The Bihar cabinet on Wednesday (August 12, 2026) gave its nod to develop 300 ‘stand-alone’ private teacher education institutions (B.Ed.) operating in Bihar into multidisciplinary degree colleges.
The decision will add another 300 additional degree colleges which will offer undergraduate programmes in Arts, Science, Commerce, and other disciplines along with teacher education (B.Ed.) and skill-based courses, Cabinet Secretariat Department’s Secretary Mohammad Sohail said in a post cabinet briefing.
The decision was taken in accordance with the National Education Policy (NEP), 2020, and the guidelines of the National Council for Teacher Education (NCTE), he added.
The new academic programmes will be conducted in accordance with the standards and necessary approvals prescribed by the concerned university, UGC, NCTE, and the State government, Mr. Sohail said.
The initiative will provide students with greater opportunities for higher education within their own district or nearby areas, strengthen access to higher education, and contribute to increasing the state’s Gross Enrolment Ratio (GER), he added.
Extension of Schemes
It also gave the higher education department’s proposal to extend the Bihar Student Credit Card Scheme for another five years from 2026-27 to 2030-31, Mr. Sohail said, adding that ₹950 crore has been approved to be spent in the current financial year 2026-27.
Stating 4.15 lakh students have been benefitted from the SCC scheme, he said this decision will provide students in the State with greater opportunities for higher education, strengthen access to higher education, and promote an increase in the State’s Gross Enrolment Ratio (GER).
A step towards connecting Bihar’s youth with new age employment opportunities, the cabinet also extended the period of ‘Kushal Yuva Programme’ from 2026-27 to 2030-31 under ‘Seven Nischay Part-3’.
It approved ₹430.08 crore for imparting training to youth in future skills such as AI, drones, solar, networking, digital marketing, banking, telecom, foreign languages, and entrepreneurship, the Secretary said and added that it will directly create 6,436 employment opportunities and train 2,57,440 lakh youth annually.
Financial Assistance
In another decision, the cabinet also approved an estimated expenditure of ₹1,000 crore for a period of one year under “Pradhan Mantri Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana”, Mr. Sohail said, adding that the State government would give ₹10,000 per kilowatt subject to a maximum of ₹20,000 through DBT as financial assistance to the residential consumers for installing rooftop solar panels.
The State government’s financial assistance will be given in addition to the central government’s share, he added.
It also decided to set up Compressed Biogas (CBG) plants in four municipal corporations of Gaya Ji, Muzaffarpur, Bhagalpur and Biharsharif (Nalanda) for providing a sustainable solution for waste management by converting organic waste into a valuable renewable energy source, Mr. Sohail said.
The government would give 10 acres of land for a period of 25 years to IOCL, HPCL, BPCL and GAIL for the purpose, he said adding that CBG plants process organic waste and convert it into a valuable energy resource, thereby improving waste management.
Restriction lifted
In yet another decision, the cabinet also lifted the restriction imposed on the purchase, sale, and transfer of land in the notified Greenfield Satellite Cities following the final publication of the Development Plan, Mr. Sohail said.
In addition, the Bihar Urban Development Authority will have the power to lift the restriction on the purchase, sale, and transfer of land after the publication of the draft Development Plan.
The cabinet also approved the Youth, Employment and Skill Development Department’s proposal to amend the admission process for the State’s Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs) and to conduct admissions to 50% of the total sanctioned seats in private Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs through the Bihar Combined Entrance Competitive Examination Board (BCECEB), Patna.
A total of 11 decisions were taken at cabinet meeting chaired by Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary on Wednesday (August 12, 2026).

The Supreme Court of India on Thursday (August 13, 2026) asked the union government to consider a petition filed by an apex court lawyer flagging the lack of a comprehensive statutory regime on the government’s use of “high-risk” Artificial Intelligence technology in areas affecting public access to food, health benefits, wages, pension, scholarship and grant of welfare subsidies.
A three-judge Bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant asked the government to consider the detailed petition of advocate N.K. Goswami as a representation for taking comprehensive action.
In his petition, Mr. Goswami questioned whether the government could employ AI, machine learning (ML), automated decision-making systems, risk-scoring mechanisms, biometric surveillance tools, predictive policing technologies and AI-assisted content moderation systems in crucial areas of governance affecting welfare, liberty, privacy, dignity, livelihood and speech, without a “specific statutory framework” or meaningful human oversight.
The lawyer clarified that the constitutional vice pleaded in the petition was not that technology must be prohibited.
“The vice is that technology affecting fundamental rights cannot be permitted to operate outside the discipline of the Constitution. When a citizen’s access to food, health benefits, wages, pension, scholarship, subsidy, liberty, privacy or speech is affected by an opaque automated or semi-automated system, the State must satisfy the minimum constitutional requirements,” Mr. Goswami submitted.
The petition said he was only trying to constitutionalise innovation.
“AI is no longer merely an administrative aid or technological convenience. It has begun to enter the bloodstream of governance. Public-domain official materials, policy and supporting documents show that AI/ML, automated decision-making, fraud-detection, beneficiary-verification, Aadhaar-linked authentication, data-driven de-duplication and similar algorithmic systems are being used in welfare-linked governance, from health-benefit delivery to ration-distribution optimisation to fraud-prevention,” it said.
The Chief Justice said the petition raised technical issues in the policy domain, and the court lacked the necessary technical know-how to address them.
Mr Goswami argued that the court could indeed intervene to fill the legislative gap, given the lack of any statutory mechanism governing the use of AI/ML in public welfare.
The petition had sought that the court direct the Centre to file a “complete affidavit” disclosing all existing and proposed high-risk AI systems used by Union Ministries/agencies in welfare, policing, surveillance and content regulation, together with their legal basis, vendor/agency, purpose, data categories, safeguards, grievance mechanism and audit status.

An attempt made by a railway gatekeeper at Gopurarajapuram near Papanasam in Thanjavur district to save another person from being run over by a train on Wednesday (August 12, 2026) night cost him his life.
Inquiries reveal that the gatekeeper, Rahul Kumar (30) of Keerthai hamlet, Baghpat district, Uttar Pradesh, who was posted for duty at the level crossing (LC) gate at Gopurarajapuram, saw a person heading towards the railway track while the Nagercoil-Tambaram Antyodaya Express was fast approaching the LC at around 11.45 p.m. on August 12.
Immediately, he ran towards the person and attempted to pull him to safety. However, the person was hit by the speeding train, and in the process, the gatekeeper too was killed. The identity of the person whom the railway gatekeeper attempted to save but who was also killed in the accident had yet to be identified, according to official sources.

The Congress-led United Democratic Front (UDF) government in Kerala on Thursday (August 13, 2026) edged closer to ordering a multi-angled investigation into the previous Left Democratic Front (LDF) government’s “bungled attempt” to bring the 2021 FIFA World Cup-winning Argentina team and its iconic captain, Lionel Messi, for a friendly match at Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium in Kochi in 2025.
Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan told a press conference that the State Sports Department’s preliminary inquiry into the alleged fiasco, which left football fans profoundly disappointed, revealed “very serious allegations” warranting further investigation by multiple departments and agencies.
(The charges in the report, vetted by Sports Department Special Secretary N. Prasanth, reportedly included massive service tax fraud on foreign remittances, contraventions of the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA), abuse of power resulting in loss to the public exchequer, and “shady financial transactions” involving offshore entities, among other charges.)
Mr Satheesan said the previous government “cannot not shrug off responsibility” centred around the controversy by airing “contradictory statements”.
He said several questions remain unanswered. “What was the procedure followed by the previous government to permit the private sponsor (a television news broadcasting company) to transact with the Argentine Football Association (AFA) on behalf of the State without inviting an expression of intent, a legal pre-requisite before entering into a final binding contract or agreement? Did the government examine the source of the private sponsor’s funding? Did it conduct a market price determination before contemplating a binding legal contract or agreement with the private sponsor?”, Mr Satheesan asked.
The Chief Minister said the Finance Department, which he heads, has opened an investigation into suspected GST levy evasion on foreign remittances, amounting to a projected ₹156 crore, purportedly made by the sponsor to the Argentine Football Association to secure Messi and his team’s presence in Kochi.

Congress MP Renuka Chowdhury has written to Chief Minister Revanth Reddy of the Congress-led government in Telangana, asking that the State government take a position in the Supreme Court to support the Constitutional challenges to the recently passed amendments to the Transgender Rights law that removed the right to self-identification of gender identity.
The law, passed in Parliament this March, ran into widespread protests from the transgender community across the country and had also led to resignations from members appointed to the Government’s National Council for Transgender Persons over provisions that mandate medical certification of gender identity instead of relying on self-identification.
Ms. Chowdhury, whose opposition to the amendments has been vocal, inside and outside Parliament, has now asked the Congress government in Telangana to support the challenges to the amendment that are currently being heard in the Supreme Court of India. In a letter to Mr. Reddy, the Congress’ Rajya Sabha MP from Telangana said, “I would earnestly request the Government of Telangana to extend its support to these proceedings through the office of the Learned Additional Advocate General, Shri Rajnikanth Reddy, by assisting the court in defence of the constitutional rights and dignity of transgender persons.”
In addition to this, Ms. Chowdhury has also requested the Telangana government to “carefully examine the administrative, financial and implementation implications of the new Act” for the State. She noted that this was needed to look at where the amended Act “may conflict with the State’s existing welfare architecture and its commitment to protecting the rights of transgender persons”.
Ms. Chowdhury noted in her letter to the Telangana CM that the State has “consistently stood for inclusion, social justice, and constitutional morality, and its intervention at this stage would carry both legal and moral significance.”
She also noted that during the debate on the amendments in Rajya Sabha, the Congress party had strongly opposed the legislation on the grounds that it undermined the principles of dignity, equality, and self-identification recognised by the Supreme Court, and “strikes at the heart of the guarantees under Articles 14, 15, 19, and 21 of our Constitution”.
At the time the Bill was being introduced and discussed, a delegation of trans activists from across the country had also met with the Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha, Rahul Gandhi and Congress leader Priyanka Gandhi Vadra in New Delhi, following which the official account of the Indian National Congress had posted a statement saying that Mr. Gandhi reiterated that the “Congress party stands firmly with the rights and dignity of transgender persons and will oppose the Bill in Parliament”.
Soon after the amendments to the Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act were passed, several challenges to it were filed before the Supreme Court of India, which has issued notice in these matters to the Union government. The next hearing in the case is scheduled for August 17.

The long-delayed Joka-Esplanade metro in Kolkata has seen a breakthrough as the final lap of tunneling work was completed on Tuesday (August 11, 2026). This is the second and final tunnel in this line, the previous one had reached completion on July 10.

The Tunnel Boring Machine (TBM) ‘Divya’ successfully achieved breakthrough at Victoria Metro Station around Tuesday (August 11) noon. Just a month back, TBM ‘Durga’ had already achieved breakthrough for the first tunnel at the same station.

TBM Durga started boring the 1.75 km tunnel between Kidderpore and Victoria in July 2025, and TBM Divya started the work on October 2025.

A parliamentary panel has flagged a "drastic decline" in the number of schools and students as education level rises, noting that nearly 73% students drop out before finishing higher secondary.
The recommendation is part of the Tenth Report (Eighteenth Lok Sabha) of the Committee on Estimates (2026-27) on "Budget and Policy aspects for providing Affordable and Quality Education in the Country including Review of Central Board of Secondary Education", presented to Lok Sabha on Wednesday (August 12, 2026).
The committee noted that the number of schools at Secondary and Higher Secondary levels are very less when compared with the number of schools at Primary and Upper Primary levels.
It said as per the Unified District Information System for Education (UDISE) 2024-25, out of the total 10,92,671 schools, including all the government and government aided schools, there are 9,11,032 schools at primary level, 4,12,805 schools at upper primary level, 1,61,808 schools at secondary level, and only 90,866 schools at higher secondary level in the country.
With regard to the number of students enrolled, in primary classes there are 6,18,45,033 students and 4,08,93,978 students in upper primary classes from 6 to 8, which reduces to 2,36,68,220 in secondary, and further reduces to 1,64,17,949 in higher secondary classes.
Drastic decline in number of schools
"The committee are concerned to note this drastic decline in number of schools and students as education levels rises," it said.
"From the above information, the Committee note that out of over 1 million (10 lakhs) government schools, the vast majority are only primary schools, and nearly 73% of students drop out before finishing higher secondary," it added.
The committee strongly urged the Ministry to prioritise upgrading existing primary and secondary schools into full higher secondary schools to ensure a high school is physically accessible to students belonging to different communities and to arrest student drop-off rate.
"The Committee are of the view that there is an urgent need to increase the number of schools at secondary and higher secondary levels," it said.
Considering that education is placed in the Concurrent List of the Constitution with most schools under the jurisdiction of the State Governments and UT Administration, the committee desired the Ministry to impress upon all the State/UT Government to take steps for setting up of more secondary and higher secondary schools so as to increase the enrolment of students in the country.
Gap in the availability of CwSN friendly infrastructure
On facilities for Divyang students to achieve inclusive education across the country, the committee flagged a severe gap in the availability of CwSN friendly infrastructure, noting that more than half of schools across the country are devoid of CwSN-friendly infrastructure.
The committee noted that in order to achieve the objective of inclusive education, the Ministry of Education provides financial support to State Governments and Union Territories to strengthen infrastructure and human resources for inclusive education of Divyang students under the Samagra Shiksha scheme.
To improve physical accessibility of schools, the scheme includes specific provisions for the creation of barrier-free and differently-abled-friendly infrastructure, such as ramps, handrails and accessible toilets, so that children with disabilities can move safely and participate fully in school activities.
Though the committee appreciated the vision of the Ministry, it noted that as per UDISE+ 2024-25, out of total 14,71,437 schools at national level, only 5,23,143 schools have CwSN (Children with special needs) toilets, and only 8,08,466 schools have ramps with handrails.
During 2024-25, a budget of ₹482 lakh was allocated for construction of 186 CwSN toilets, however only ₹2.60 lakh was actually utilised with no progress in physical targets.
"The severe gap in the availability of CwSN friendly infrastructure shows that more than half of the schools across the country are devoid of CwSN friendly infrastructure," the committee said.
The committee further noted that under the financial support for new special educators, only ₹80.50 lakh was utilised against a budgetary grant (elementary section) of ₹962 lakh.
It also noted that a meagre progress was achieved in the area of recruiting/retaining special educators for CwSN students.
On the Ministry's approach to promoting education for Divyang children, the committee noted that it is rights based, inclusive and holistic.
It said The Rights of Persons with Disabilities (RPnD) Act, 2016 provides that children with benchmark disabilities are entitled to free education up to the age of 18 years.
The NEP 2020 emphasises a Zero Rejection Policy for children with disabilities, ensuring that no child is denied schooling on account of disability. The policy also underscores the importance of preparing and training teachers to handle inclusive classrooms effectively, it said.
"In view of the above, the Committee strongly recommend the Ministry to adhere to yearly targets of budget utilisation and execution of CwSN related projects in a time bound manner," it said.
The committee recommended the Ministry provide safe and accessible infrastructure to Divyang students in a time-bound manner to achieve the objective of inclusivity in education.
The Ministry should also assess the requirement of special educators across the country and complete their recruitment at the earliest, it said.

Madhya Pradesh has received investment proposals worth ₹8,635 crore across various sectors during the Investment Dialogue held in Ahmedabad, Gujarat. These proposals are expected to create more than 5,785 employment opportunities. Chief Minister Dr. Mohan Yadav addressed leading industrialists and investors from across the country at the Mega Investment Dialogue— Interactive Session on Investment Opportunities in Madhya Pradesh — held in Ahmedabad on Wednesday, August 12, 2026.
Chief Minister Dr. Yadav said Madhya Pradesh offers immense opportunities for business, setting up new industrial units, expanding existing ones and scaling up operations. Investment in Madhya Pradesh has always been a profitable proposition. Welcoming investors from across the country on behalf of the State’s 8.5 crore people, the Chief Minister said the State Government would provide every possible facility, security and support to investors.
The Chief Minister said, referring to the development drive underway across the country under Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s leadership to build a self-reliant India, Madhya Pradesh’s new industrial policies are receiving appreciation from the industry. He said, “For running an industry, what is primarily needed is a sound policy, good intent and a supportive government. You will find all three in Madhya Pradesh.”
Inviting Gujarat’s industry leaders to the upcoming Global Investors Summit-2027 in Bhopal, Chief Minister Dr. Yadav said, “You have the experience, and we have the opportunities. If our opportunities are combined with your experience, together we can create history.” He called upon industrialists to become partners in Madhya Pradesh’s growth journey and said, “Come, invest in Madhya Pradesh without hesitation and with an open heart, and become part of this historic journey of development.”
Land, power and water: No concern for investors
Chief Minister Dr. Yadav said investors in Madhya Pradesh need not worry about electricity, water or land. Industrial land is available on lease at concessional rates, the State has adequate water reserves and surplus power, and plug-and-play zones are being developed. As many as 48 new industrial parks are being developed across nearly 19,000 acres. The Chief Minister said, describing the single-window system as “end of problems, instant service,” that solutions to every hurdle are available on a single digital platform. Highlighting seamless connectivity as a major strength of Madhya Pradesh, he said the State has a road network of more than 5 lakh kilometres, strong rail connectivity, eight airports, six inland container depots, expressways and highways. He added that trained and skilled manpower is also readily available in the State.
Madhya Pradesh and Gujarat are twin brothers
Chief Minister Dr. Yadav said, highlighting the industrial potential and scope for high-quality mutual cooperation between Madhya Pradesh and Gujarat, the two States are like twin brothers. Gujarat brings technological expertise, business acumen and industrial experience, while Madhya Pradesh offers abundant water resources, a large land bank and a strategic logistics advantage due to its central location. Combining these unique strengths can create a new chapter of industrial development in the region.
Chief Minister Dr. Yadav said Madhya Pradesh offers vast opportunities for Gujarat’s petrochemical, chemical, textile, pharma, food processing and automobile sectors. The large petrochemical refinery in Bina, the state-of-the-art Medical Device Park being developed over 360 acres in Ujjain, PM MITRA Parks in Dhar and Navsari, and the strong automobile base in Pithampur further strengthen the prospects for industrial cooperation between the two States. Kerala Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan on Thursday (August 13, 2026) denied making any request to Meta to remove news items related to him or the Congress-led United Democratic Front (UDF) government from Facebook.
The Opposition Left Democratic Front (LDF) had on Wednesday accused the UDF government of clamping down an “undeclared social media emergency” by allegedly removing several posts as well as news reports related to the arrest of Youth Congress leaders on synthetic drug peddling charges. Leader of the Opposition Pinarayi Vijayan on Thursday posted screenshots of the removal of news reports of his own statements on one of the accused being close to Mr. Satheesan.
Speaking to mediapersons after the Cabinet meeting, Mr. Satheesan said no one from his office or the government had made any request to Meta to remove posts.
“We have no idea how Meta is deciding on these things. Three news items favourable to me, including one on the Latin Archbishop’s praise for the government’s interventions in the coastal sector, have also been removed. This has been happening in other States too after a meeting of Meta officials with the Union government recently. The only request I have given to Meta till now is to give us access to the official CMO Keralam page on Instagram. But even after two months, no decision has been taken on it,” said Mr. Satheesan.
He asked the aggrieved news channels to “proceed with a complaint” to Meta. “The government will support you in this. I am only happy if these news items are reinstated. I don’t have the false impression that social media can be silenced by removing a few posts,” he said.
All posts and news reports which were removed were from platforms managed by Meta.
As per the screenshots shared by Mr. Vijayan, access to multiple news reports from the Facebook pages of News Malayalam 24X7, Reporter Live, Kairali News and Deshabhimani were restricted in India as per “legal requirements” under the Information Technology (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Rules, 2021. Such regional blocking of posts are usually carried out under demands from the government. Some social media users also posted that their earlier posts with videos and photographs of one of the MDMA case accused with the Chief Minister were removed.
Regarding allegations of his proximity to the accused in the MDMA racket bust, Mr. Satheesan said he knew K.H. Mohammed Hussain and P.A. Abdul Salam, but came to know about their connection to drug rackets “only after their arrest” during the Operation Toofan anti-drug drive.
“I first came in touch with Hussain, a Youth Congress worker, after he was injured in the police action during the LDF government’s Nava Kerala Sadas. I consoled him over the phone and promised that I would visit his house. Later when I visited the panchayat, I paid a visit to him. After that we met 3-4 times at various places, but no one had any idea about his drug racket connections,” said Mr. Satheesan.

A new survey in Arunachal Pradesh has documented recurring experiences of widespread harassment of members of the LGBTQIA+ community in the State.
Also read | On India’s rainbow trail | Queer-focused walks are finding an audience in the country
According to the Itanagar-based HimKai Research Institute (HRI), the pestering or provocation has led to identity concealment, discrimination-related distress, and low confidence in institutional protection among the LGBTQIA+ respondents in the State.
LGBTQIA+ expands to Lesbian, Gay, Bisexual, Transgender, Queer or Questioning, Intersex, and Asexual.
The HRI conducted the anonymous online survey between June 2 and August 2. It received 62 submissions, one of which was excluded during geographic eligibility and data-quality screening because the self-reported home district could not be mapped in Arunachal Pradesh.
“Among the 61 respondents included in the analysis, 49.2% said they hid their gender identity or sexual orientation most of the time or always because of fear of discrimination or violence. Half of valid respondents said they felt accepted within their family rarely or never, while 44.3% said they felt safe in their local community rarely or never,” the HRI report said.
“Experiences of harassment and discrimination were reported across several settings. Some 91.8% of respondents reported verbal harassment at least rarely, while 52.5% reported physical threats or violence at least rarely. Among valid responses, 85.0% reported discrimination in school or college at least rarely, and 63.2% reported workplace discrimination,” it said.
The survey also found that 72.9% of valid respondents felt compelled to change their behaviour or appearance sometimes or more often to retain work or education. A further 57.9% said their identity affected access to employment or income opportunities at least rarely.
Religious, cultural exclusion
“Mental wellbeing emerged as a significant concern. Among valid responses, 76.7% reported experiencing stress, anxiety or emotional distress related to discrimination sometimes or more often, including 48.3% who experienced it most of the time or always. Access to mental-health or peer support was uneven: 41.0% said such support was available most of the time or always, while 36.1% said it was available rarely or never,” the report said.
The findings also point to a gap between awareness of rights and confidence in institutions. While 56.7% of valid respondents agreed that they were aware of their legal rights, 63.3% disagreed that laws and policies adequately protect LGBTQIA+ persons, and 66.7% disagreed that police and authorities respond sensitively to LGBTQIA+ issues.
Religion, culture and social belonging received particularly cautious assessments. Some 72.1% did not agree that religion or faith practices are accepting of LGBTQIA+ persons. More than half disagreed that their identity is compatible with their cultural or tribal background or that local traditions allow space for diverse identities, with 51.7% of valid respondents disagreeing that they feel a sense of belonging in society.
Healthcare emerged as a comparatively more positive area. Among valid respondents, 56.7% said that they felt comfortable accessing healthcare most of the time or always, and 75.0% said healthcare providers treated them with respect most of the time or always.
“Friends were the most frequently reported source of support, mentioned by 37 respondents, followed by LGBTQIA+ networks, mentioned by 12.
Six respondents mentioned. Awareness and sensitisation were the most common single priority identified for improving LGBTQIA+ lives in Arunachal Pradesh, followed by legal protection,” the report said.
HRI director Ranju Dodum said the study was intended to begin building locally grounded evidence on experiences that are often discussed without adequate data.
“LGBTQIA+ experiences in Arunachal Pradesh cannot simply be assumed from national conversations. Family, community, tribal identity, religion, education and employment all shape how people experience acceptance and safety here. This is a baseline study and its numbers must be read with methodological caution, but they point to questions that deserve deeper research and serious public discussion,” he said.
The report recommends sustained sensitisation programmes in schools, colleges, workplaces, healthcare institutions, police and public administration; confidential mechanisms for reporting discrimination; stronger mental-health and peer-support systems; safe community spaces; more inclusive education and workplace practices; and locally grounded engagement with families, community institutions and faith leaders.
The survey sample was predominantly young, with 90.2% of respondents between 18 and 35 years.

The Greater Chennai Corporation’s (GCC) property tax reassessment drive has drawn heavy backlash over sharp increases and a lack of prior consultation and transparency.
A GCC official said the revised tax was based on self-declared property area. The first revision was carried out in 2018, followed by a major one in 2022, but the collection was subsequently paused. The revised rate should have been collected 2022 onwards, and is now being implemented, he said.
T.K. Shanmugam, chairman of the Federation of North Chennai Residents’ Welfare Associations (FNCRWA), said a resident, who had been paying a property tax of ₹295, was demanded ₹3,255 following the reassessment, without receiving any explanation. Mr. Shanmugam said the residents were not given details such as the rate per square foot or the basis for the revised assessment.
He further questioned whether the residents would be able to approach the Revenue Department officials to raise objections, given the large number of properties involved.
He said many houses in North Chennai had undergone additions over the years that may not have been reflected in earlier assessments. However, he criticised the manner in which such changes were being reassessed using only drone and GIS-based methods, without manual confirmation.
Many also took to social media, saying the sudden move and close deadline had put several residents between a rock and a hard place.
Sandhya Vedullapalli, secretary of the Federation of Anna Nagar Residents’ Associations, said that for her, the tax was revised from ₹895 to ₹1,835 — a 100% increase. She alleged that in an apartment complex, only one flat had received the reassessment notice, raising questions about uniformity in the exercise.
For Vijaykumar, who owns a space in Mogappair, the rate went up from ₹6,500 for six months to over ₹31,000, nearly a five-fold increase. “I am yet to raise an objection. Such sudden increases could affect businesses, especially small ones,” he said.
‘Received information’
Meanwhile, Tiruvottiyur CPI(M) councillor R. Jayaraman said several residents in his ward had received information regarding the revision.
He said the GCC had taken the decision without passing a resolution in the Council. “There was no prior information. When there is an online gateway to register complaints about all issues, there ought to be one for this too. We will put forth our objection in the next Council meeting,” Mr. Jayaraman said.
Pointing out that the earlier property tax increases had contributed to public dissatisfaction with the previous regime, CPI(M)’s G. Selva said the new government should reconsider the decision.
Some residents of Thoraipakkam and Neelankarai had received information about the revision, A. Francis of Thoraipakkam Residents’ Welfare Association said.
Buffer zone
Kumararaja of Velachery said some residents of Tansi Nagar, Annai Indira Nagar, Vijay Nagar, Mahatma Gandhi Street, and Nehru Street had received reassessment notices.
He said the properties in these localities had been classified as having “zero value”, as they fell within the buffer zone of the Pallikaranai marshland. Since further development was not possible in the area, he questioned the basis for revising the property tax, and said the decision should be reconsidered.
A resident of Nanganallur said: “The GCC has increased the tax for the apartment owned by my bedridden mother. From the earlier half-yearly rate of ₹900, the tax has now been revised to ₹3,300. The property is held exclusively by my mother aged 80. As she has been bedridden since last year, her family pension is not adequate to meet the mounting medical expenses. Either the basic street rate should be reduced or it should be reduced on a par with core areas of Chennai. Nanganallur has higher rates than some core areas,” he said.
Arun, a resident of Adambakkam, welcomed the move, saying it corrected under-assessed properties rather than imposing a uniform hike. Though he agreed that a reassessment of under-valued properties would increase revenue for the GCC, he said there should have been greater transparency and awareness among the public.
Chairman of the Standing Committee on Taxation and Finance Sarbajaya Das told The Hindu that the decision had been taken by the Commissioner and the Deputy Commissioner (Revenue and Finance).
She said the reassessment had initially been intended for commercial buildings, followed by around 6,000 residential properties. The committee had not been informed that residential properties would also be reassessed under the new government, she said.
Stating that the Council had not been informed that objections could be raised, Ms. Das said they would demand a portal to address the issue and greater transparency at the next meeting of the Standing Committee on August 23 or 24.
She added that the GCC was facing a severe fund crunch, with no maintenance or ward development funds released and a liability of ₹2,000 crore.
GCC’s response
The GCC has issued notices to three lakh assessees for under-assessment of property tax. It expects to generate an additional revenue of ₹83 crore per annum from the revision of property tax on under-assessed properties.
Corporation Commissioner G.S. Sameeran, in a statement, said: “The change is only for properties that were under-assessed and those that were converted to commercial. It is based on GIS, satellite imagery, other government databases, and the owner’s self-declaration of area. The assessee can request remeasurement and reconsideration to RDCs. The same will be disposed of within a month,” he said.

From seven deceased donor organ donations in its first year, to 266 in a single year, Tamil Nadu has come a long way in 17 years. Behind the rise is a gradual shift in public perception, shaped by sustained awareness efforts, measures to build confidence, and trust and improvements in the State’s transplant infrastructure and systems.
The numbers tell a compelling story of how far the State has come with regard to organ donation and transplantation. Since 2008, the highest number of deceased organ donors was recorded in 2024, when Tamil Nadu had 268 donors. In 2025, there were 266 donors - 211 men and 55 women. A total of 1,476 organs were utilised - 856 major organs and 620 minor organs and tissues that year, according to the Transplant Authority of Tamil Nadu’s data.
On World Organ Donation Day, which falls on August 13, experts revisit the milestones, the lessons learnt and the road ahead.
How it worked
J. Amalorpavanathan, founder-member secretary, Transplant Authority of Tamil Nadu, said, “When we started in 2008, the concept of brain death was scarcely understood among healthcare professionals. A few coordinated brain death certifications were happening sporadically, with MOHAN Foundation [an NGO] coordinating around two to three such cases a year in a few city hospitals. The State government had decided to start the Cadaver Transplant Programme (CTP), and the groundwork began in April. We went on to issue 10 government orders. It was in September that year that the parents of 15-year-old Hithendran (who had sustained severe injuries in a road accident and was declared brain dead) decided to donate his organs. The CTP was launched in October 2008, and Hithendran’s case helped organ donation pick up in the State.”
Recalling his visits to all districts, he said that initially, there was reluctance among doctors. “But whenever I interacted with the general public, I found a sense of receptiveness. In fact, though they had questions and sought clarifications, I found the least resistance among them. We slowly convinced healthcare professionals to certify brain death. We had seven donations in the first year, and crossed 180 in a year in eight years. Though the number of organ donations dipped during the COVID-19 pandemic, it picked up again thereafter,” he pointed out.
Families coming forward
Sunil Shroff, managing trustee of MOHAN Foundation, said there had been a tremendous improvement in awareness levels over the years. “Earlier, we found it hard to obtain consent for organ donation. Now, many families are coming forward to donate. In States such as Tamil Nadu and Telangana, where awareness is relatively high, I think that 10 to 15% of families come forward to donate. This is a paradigm shift,” he observed.
About 72% of deceased organ donations in the country happens in five States - Tamil Nadu, Telangana, Maharashtra, Gujarat and Karnataka. Southern states, he said, have done well in terms of creating awareness on organ donations.
Compared with other States, awareness about organ donation was far higher in Tamil Nadu. Unpublished data from a major transplant centre showed that the acceptance rate was 70 to 75% after the first counselling and increased by another 10% following the second counselling, a senior doctor noted.
“According to me, awareness creation can be approached in two ways. One is to organise awareness campaigns and sessions and encourage people to take pledges. In T.N.’s experience, we found that news about successful donations, honour walks for donors and giving due recognition to donors were more effective awareness tools. Since October 2023 (the former DMK government issued an order to accord State honours to the mortal remains of deceased donors in September 2023), more than 800 such State honours have been accorded. News about successful donations and the utilisation of donated organs has proved to be a more effective way of creating awareness,” Dr. Shroff explained.
What’s needed now
Dr. Amalorpavanathan said that the involvement of people and healthcare professionals along with government support has helped improve organ donation in the State. “Successive governments did their best to take the programme forward. We have well developed infrastructure and doctors who are willing to go the extra mile,” he said.
However, this brings in another perspective. “We have an unacceptable number of brain deaths due to the high number of road traffic accidents. We need to reduce accidents and make roads safe. Developed countries have moved towards Donation after Circulatory Death (DCD), and we should also explore this possibility. In living donor organ transplants, we should promote swap transplants in a big way,” he noted.
At a recent press conference on a heart transplant in a young patient with Dilated Cardiomyopathy, Rajeev Thilak Chellasamy, heart transplant surgeon at SIMS Hospital, Chennai, elaborated on DCD. He noted that India has a long waiting list for transplants, and has traditionally relied on donations following brain death, while DCD was not ethically approved in the country. In DCD, the practice of which has been around for nearly 10 to 15 years, the heart is connected to a perfusion system. DCD numbers have increased in North America. If considered, it is a viable opportunity to increase the pool of donor hearts. The number of people dying while on the waiting list has increased and this needs to be addressed, he said.
Dr. Shroff called for establishing green corridors in hospitals for seamless integration of organ donation processes so that there are no missed opportunities. Similarly, every hospital should have nodal officers in place, he said.

Mr. Muthyala Raju assured the Minister that a special action plan would be prepared for the conservation of archaeological heritage and development of museums.

He asserted that the policy will connect every section of society- particularly youth, women, farmers, entrepreneurs, and disadvantaged communities- with the cooperative movement, thereby creating new avenues for self-reliance, entrepreneurship, and collective prosperity.
Bihar State vegetable processing and marketing scheme
The department has set a target to construct 350 panchayat-level vegetable collection centres and 50 block-level infrastructure facilities, Mr. Yadav said and added that Primary Vegetable Producer Cooperative Societies (PVCSs) have been set up in all the 534 blocks of the State. Each PVCS will be provided ₹2 lakh, while nine vegetable federations will get ₹10 lakh per federation as working capital to expand their businesses.
The Department has already approved various schemes worth ₹106.39 crore for creating better infrastructure facility for collection of vegetables, apart from providing better transportation and marketing arrangement, he said.
“We are continuously working to ensure that Bihar’s vegetables reach every plate. For this, farmers are being encouraged on a large scale. Soon, vegetable booths, on the lines of Sudha Dairy booths, will be opened at various locations through VegFed,” he said, adding that this will create new employment opportunities and significantly benefit farmers engaged in vegetable production at the local level.
Crop Insurance benefits to begin from Rabi Season
The implementation of the Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana in the State has been approved from the Rabi season of financial year 2026-27. Under the scheme, farmers will be assured compensation equivalent to their agricultural costs. Farmers will have to pay only a very small premium, while both the State and central governments will contribute their respective shares towards the premium.

After days of deliberations — amid hectic lobbying for portfolios and attempts by Congress legislators to get inducted into the Cabinet — the D.K. Shivakumar-led Congress government finally managed to allocate ministries on the eve of the Monsoon Session to 19 newly inducted Ministers. Two senior Ministers, who had expressed unhappiness over earlier allocations, were also given different portfolios.
Senior Minister K.H. Muniyappa, who was earlier miffed at being continued as Food and Civil Supplies Minister after he had sought Social Welfare, has managed to prevail over the party leadership. Ramalinga Reddy, who was upset at not being given Bengaluru Development and instead given Water Resources Ministry, has been allocated Forests, Ecology and Environment. Besides, Health and Family Welfare Minister U.T. Khader has been given the additional responsibility of Minority Welfare, Haj and Wakf.
The Chief Minister has retained the Law and Parliamentary Affairs besides all other unallocated portfolios.
At a time when the State is facing challenges over deficit rainfall and the farming community is in distress, the Agriculture portfolio has been given to P.M. Narendraswamy, and the Major and Medium Irrigation portfolio has gone to N. Cheluvarayaswamy, both hailing from Mandya district. Puttaranga Shetty, from Chamarajanagar district, has been allocated Animal Husbandry and Sericulture.
The portfolio allocation from the Governor’s office came on Wednesday (August 12, 2026) evening as the Ministers huddled to strategise for the legislature session commencing on Thursday (August 13, 2026). The newly inducted Ministers with their portfolios will have their first full Cabinet meeting on Thursday (August 13, 2026) afternoon.
The allocation comes even as the government will be headed to the session without a woman Minister, though the Chief Minister has promised that the remaining one berth will be filled by a woman legislator. The portfolio allocation took Mr. Shivakumar nearly 10 days to finalise after multiple visits to Delhi, meetings with disgruntled legislators who missed out on berths, and pressure from the Ministers for portfolio.
Some of the Ministers have been continued in the same portfolios that they had held in the previous government under former Chief Minister Siddaramaiah. They include B.Z. Zameer Ahmed (Housing), Madhu Bangarappa (School Education and Literacy), Shivaraj Tangadagi (Backward Classes Welfare and Kannada and Culture), Santosh Lad (Labour and Employment), and S.S. Mallikarjun (Mines and Geology).
Some Ministers have got portfolios which they handled earlier. Basavaraj Rayaraddi has been given Higher Education, which he had held in Mr. Siddaramaiah’s first tenure as Chief Minister, and Laxman Savadi has been given Cooperation, which he managed earlier during his stint as Minister in the BJP government.
K.S. Basanthappa, a first-time legislator from Mayakonda, has been given Muzrai, Fisheries, Ports, and Inland Water. B. Nagendra, who has been in the eye of the storm over his cases connected with multi-crore embezzlement in the Karnataka State Valmiki Development Corporation and whose resignation the Opposition parties are demanding, has been allocated Planning and Statistics.
Food and Civil Supplies and Consumer Affairs has been handed to Rizwan Arshad, Excise to K.M. Shivalinge Gowda, Minor Irrigation, Science and Technology to Ajay Singha, Scheduled Tribe Welfare to T. Raghumurthy, Sugar and Textiles to Rudrappa Lamani, Municipal Administration to H.C. Balakrishna, and Small Scale Industries and Public Enterprises to Vijayanand Kashappanavar.

Jammu, Aug 13: Two earthquakes of moderate magnitude jolted the Union Territory of Ladakh within a span of nearly four hours on Thursday, triggering fear among residents.
According to the National Centre for Seismology (NCS), the first and stronger tremor, measuring 5.5 magnitude, struck at 6.05 am, with its epicentre located at a latitude of 36.88 degrees north and longitude of 74.402 degrees east.
It occurred at a depth of 10 kilometres in Ladakh's Leh, it said.
Another earthquake of 4.3 magnitude occurred at 9.54 am, at latitude 36.76 degrees north and longitude of 75.326 degrees east, also at a depth of 10 kilometres in Leh, the NCS said.
Both earthquakes were recorded in the Leh region and occurred within a span of about four hours.
There were no immediate reports of loss of life or damage to property.
The back-to-back tremors triggered concern among residents in the region, which falls in a seismically active zone.

Natarajan Chandrasekaran, the chairman of Tata Sons, who announced his exit from the position at the end of his tenure in February next, will be known for giving new directions to the Tata Group and putting big bets on high technology-oriented businesses after taking over the reins in 2017.
Tata Sons chairman N. Chandrasekaran to step down in February 2027
The technocrat who helmed Tata Consultancy Services for eight years before getting selected to lead the group under challenging circumstances, steered the conglomerate through unchartered territories making massive investments in semiconductors, electronics manufacturing, consumer Internet platform, mobile technology and battery giga-factories, which are new for the salt-to-software group.
It was under him that the Tata group expanded its aviation presence through the acquisition of Air India with a bold attempt to build a global airline out of India.
Of course, as the first non-Parsi to lead the Group, he had the complete backing of his mentor former Tata Sons Chairman & Tata Trusts chairman Ratan Tata till the latter’s death in October 2024.
N. Chandrasekaran to step down as chairman of Tata Sons | 5 key questions answered
After the sudden ouster of former Tata Sons Chairman Cyrus Mistry following a boardroom battle, Mr. Chandrasekaran, joined the board of Tata Sons in October 2016 and appointed chairman in January 2017 after a selection committee ratified his candidature.
“At that time, he was the most successful CEO of the Tata Group and was the natural choice,” said a Tata Group veteran who was a part of the selection committee.
Long stint with TCS
Before becoming the Chairman of Tata Sons, he was the Chief Executive of TCS, a company where he started as a trainee in 1987 and served for 30 years, including eight years as CEO, until 2017.
Under his leadership, TCS became the country’s most valuable company, and he led it’s growth in overseas markets amid adverse conditions.
If Mr. Ratan Tata consolidated the Group’s position in key businesses through significant international acquisitions and increased Tata Sons’ holding in Group companies apart from keeping a tight control over the conglomerate, Mr. Chandrasekaran would be known for ensuring synergy, simplicity and scale through his “One Tata” strategy.
He was seen driving transformation of the Tata group towards a sustainable future.
Considered very close to Mr. Ratan Tata, he is believed to have come in the crossfire from the internal squabble in Tata Trusts that controls 66% of Tata Sons’ holding and takes key decisions on the running of the holding company.
Noel takes over
Noel Tata, the half-brother of Ratan Tata, became chairman of Tata Trusts in October 2024 soon after his brother’s passing away and since then, the regime change had it’s effects on the affairs at both Tata Trusts and Tata Sons.
While many of Mr. Ratan Tata loyalists quit from both Tata Trusts and Tata Sons some more were likely to exit soon, according to Tata Group insiders.
The departure of Mr. Chandrasekaran is due to lack of clarity on his extension is part of this.
In his statement issued on Wednesday he had stated that though his third five-year term from February 2027 was cleared by Tata Trusts and the nomination & remuneration committee of Tata Sons approved of it, one board member [Noel Tata] did not support it, leading to uncertainties.
Mr. Chandrasekaran was reportedly tasked to find a way for not listing Tata Sons as demanded by the Shapoorji Pallonji Group which has about 18% stake in Tata Sons and as per RBI norms.
He was also required by the board to reduce the losses at several companies which were bleeding the group, including Air India and Tata Digital.
For almost 10 years he piloted the Group amidst several challenges, including the Air India plane crash, cyberattack at JLR and cash burn at Tata Nue to name a few, and had to go leaving an unfinished agenda through he was all set to continue for five more years.
By announcing his exit six months ahead of the end of his tenure, he, someone who had worked with the group for nearly 40 years, demonstrated his loyalty to the group which can find his successor well in time to fill the position.
Born in 1963, Mr Chandrasekaran is a Bachelor in Applied Sciences and holds Masters in Computer Applications.
A Padma Bhushan, he is also the recipient of France’ highest civilian award Légion d’Honneur, in 2023. In 2025, he was conferred Honorary Knight of the Most Excellent Order of the British Empire.
He has been awarded several honorary doctorates by leading Universities in India and internationally, including an honorary Doctor of Letters from Macquarie University, Australia, Doctor Honoris Causa by Nyenrode University, The Netherlands, and Doctor of Letters from the Regional Engineering College, Trichy, Tamil Nadu.
He is also the author of Bridgital Nation, a book on harnessing technological disruptions to bring Indians closer to their dreams.
He is an avid photographer, and a passionate long-distance marathon runner. He is a Six Star Finisher of the World Marathon Majors and continues to champion fitness.
He lives in Mumbai, with his wife Lalitha, and they have a son.
He also chairs the Boards of several group operating companies, including Tata Steel Limited, Tata Motors Limited, Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles Limited, The Tata Power Company Limited, Air India Limited, Tata Consumer Products Limited, The Indian Hotels Company Limited.

Heavy rain lashed Odisha for the last 24 hours as the low-pressure area in the Bay of Bengal has become "well marked", the IMD said on Thursday (August 13, 2026).
The IMD has issued a “red warning” (take action) of very heavy to extremely heavy rainfall across Odisha.
The national weather agency in its morning message said, "The well-marked low-pressure area over North Bay of Bengal and adjoining Bangladesh-West Bengal coast moved northwestwards. It is likely to continue to move northwestwards across Gangetic West Bengal towards Jharkhand and may concentrate into a depression during the next 12 hours."
A depression is a weather system stronger than a low-pressure area but less intense than a tropical cyclone.
While issuing the “red warning” of very heavy to extremely heavy rainfall across Odisha on Thursday (August 13), the IMD said that Gangetic West Bengal, Chhattisgarh and Jharkhand would also be impacted by the ongoing wet spell caused by a low-pressure system in the Bay of Bengal.
Keeping in view the weather conditions, the IMD has advised fishermen not to venture into the North Bay of Bengal and along the Odisha-West Bengal-Bangladesh coast till August 14.
According to the Meteorological Centre (MC), Bhubaneswar, the highest rainfall of 236mm has been recorded at Bhograi in Balasore district, followed by 230mm at Shyamakhuntam 215mm at Baripada in Mayurbhanj district and 204mm at Rajghat in Balasore district.
Balasore town recorded the highest rainfall of 137mm by 5.30 a.m. on Thursday (August 13), while reports of very heavy rains were received from Similipal Hills in Mayurbhanj. The very heavy rains in Mayurbhanj led to a rise in the water levels of rivers such as Budhabalanga and Jalaka in Balasore district. A large part of Balasore town has been encountering waterlogging, an official said.
Meanwhile, in the wake of the heavy rainfall since last night (August 12), the authorities declared the closure of all educational institutions in Mayurbhanj district on Thursday (August 13).
A district administration notification said that all headmasters, headmistresses, principals and teachers should attend their respective schools as usual to disseminate information about the closure to all students and their parents/guardians through available communication channels, including class WhatsApp groups, phone calls and SMS.
The Meteorological Centre Bhubaneswar said that under the impact of the low pressure, wind speeds along the Odisha coast could reach 30 to 40 kmph. Residents are advised to remain alert during thunderstorms and lightning and follow weather advisories issued by the authorities.
